text:
anya: Heads-up — customer reported cross-region mismatch: their session was resident-EU but proxy kept routing to us-east after a mobile handoff. Logs attached, looks like affinity persisted but tenant-residency checked true earlier. :thinking:

sam: Can you paste a minimal log snippet? was it cookie-based affinity or IP?

anya: ```
2026-03-18T09:12:03Z INFO proxy: accept request tenant=acme id=abc123 src_ip=203.0.113.54 hint=eu residency=true cookie=aff-uuid-9f
2026-03-18T09:12:33Z INFO proxy: route -> eu-primary pool=eu-1
2026-03-18T09:13:05Z INFO proxy: conn drop mobile-handoff src_ip=198.51.100.2
2026-03-18T09:13:08Z INFO proxy: new request tenant=acme id=abc124 src_ip=198.51.100.2 hint=eu residency=true cookie=aff-uuid-9f
2026-03-18T09:13:08Z INFO proxy: route -> us-east pool=us-e-3
```

anya: Notice cookie still present but we routed to us-east. Looks like our pool selector used cookie->pool mapping, but pool had been marked draining and the fallback chosen ignored residency hint.

jordan: Oof. So two things: (1) cookie affinity mapping didn't include residency stamp, (2) fallback selector prefers available capacity over residency hint. That's by design for SLOs but bad for compliance.

lee: Agree. Proposal: when a tenant has residency flag=true, we should treat region hints as hard constraints for route selection, unless explicit emergency tag present. Fallback should only choose a non-resident region if (a) emergency=true OR (b) residency-check-expired TTL and user consent present.

sam: Rolling that change is risky — it can reduce capacity headroom in high load and cause throttles. We need metrics and a gradual rollout. Also mobile churn makes cookies unreliable.

anya: Thinking incremental plan:
- Phase 0: add telemetry to record (cookie_region, hint_region, chosen_pool_region, residency_flag, reason_for_fallback).
- Phase 1: prefer an explicit session token (signed region_hint) over cookie when mismatch; continue honoring cookie for backwards compat. Emit metric when mismatch occurred.
- Phase 2: enforce residency-as-constraint for 95% of traffic with canary, leave circuit-breaker allowing automatic fallback for critical paths only.

jordan: For the session token, we can issue a signed client token on first routed request that contains tenant_id and region_hint (HMAC). If token present, proxy validates and sticks to it. That avoids relying on ephemeral cookies. Need to consider token lifetime and rotation.

lee: Mobile IP churn: add a short grace window (30s) where we keep affinity for a session token but recompute pairing after. Also record geo delta (prev_ip_region vs new_ip_region) to detect device roaming.

sam: What about GDPR / consent? If residency is geo-based and customer requires data to stay in EU, we need an explicit opt-in flag per tenant. If user hasn't consented to cross-region fallback, we must queue/deny. That affects availability.

anya: Right — we should add a tenant-level field: residency_policy = {required|preferred|none} and surfaces to Console. Default for regulated customers should be required.

infra-bot: deploybot: canary rollout scheduled for proxy v1.42 with telemetry only on 2026-03-19 02:00 UTC :eyes:

jordan: Small implementation notes: keep cookie mapping but mark it deprecated; session token must be compact (base64 HMAC payload) so mobile clients can cache. Proxy should reject tokens signed by older keys and fall back to cookie-only path for those clients.

lee: Also need control-plane hooks: when Dedicated pool goes to draining, update cookie->pool mapping so cookie doesn't point to drained pool. This would reduce stale routing where cookie says eu-1 but eu-1 is gone.

sam: Cost question — enforcing residency will increase cross-region allocations and reduce packing efficiency. We should quantify cost delta before Phase 2. Add an Optimize evaluation for 1 week of synthetic traffic.

anya: I'll draft an RFC with the phases, telemetry dashboard, and sample HMAC token format. Volunteers for reviewers? @sam @jordan @lee

sam: I'll review.

jordan: happy to review too.

lee: I'll add the console schema for residency_policy.

anya: Great — putting a stub RFC link here: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/2026/multi-region-session-affinity-draft (WIP). I'll update after canary telemetry. :thumbsup:
